subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which elements are present in carbohydrates?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates contain only the elements carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.

questions.q: Proteins contain which element that is NOT found in carbohydrates or fats?
questions.explain: Proteins contain carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and, unlike carbohydrates and fats, nitrogen.

questions.q: What are the small basic units from which proteins are built?
questions.explain: Proteins are large molecules made from smaller units called amino acids.

questions.q: Fats and oils are made from which basic units?
questions.explain: Fats and oils are built from fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.q: Which large molecule is built from many glucose units?
questions.explain: Starch, glycogen and cellulose are all large molecules made from glucose.

questions.q: Which reagent is used to test a food sample for starch?
questions.explain: Iodine solution is used to test for the presence of starch.

questions.q: Benedict's solution is used to test for which substance?
questions.explain: Benedict's solution is the reagent used to test for reducing sugars.

questions.q: The biuret test is used to detect the presence of which nutrient?
questions.explain: The biuret test detects proteins.

questions.q: Why is water important in living organisms?
questions.explain: Water is important as a solvent in which many substances dissolve and are transported.

questions.q: Starch, glycogen and cellulose are all made from the same basic unit. What is it?
questions.explain: These three large carbohydrate molecules are all constructed from glucose units.

questions.q: A molecule is analysed and found to contain nitrogen as well as carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Which type of molecule is it most likely to be?
questions.explain: The presence of nitrogen indicates a protein, as carbohydrates and fats lack nitrogen.

questions.q: What colour change shows a positive result when Benedict's solution is heated with a reducing sugar?
questions.explain: On heating with a reducing sugar, Benedict's solution changes from blue to orange-red (brick-red).

questions.q: What colour change indicates a positive iodine test for starch?
questions.explain: Iodine solution changes from orange-brown to blue-black in the presence of starch.

questions.q: A positive biuret test for protein produces which colour change?
questions.explain: The biuret test changes from blue to purple (violet) when protein is present.

questions.q: In the ethanol emulsion test, a positive result for fats and oils is shown by:
questions.explain: When fats are present, the ethanol emulsion test produces a cloudy white emulsion.

questions.q: DCPIP solution becomes decolourised (loses its blue colour) in the presence of which substance?
questions.explain: Vitamin C decolourises blue DCPIP solution, turning it colourless.

questions.q: A student adds iodine solution to a food sample and it turns blue-black. What can be concluded?
questions.explain: A blue-black colour with iodine solution shows that starch is present.

questions.q: After heating a food sample with Benedict's solution, the mixture stays blue. What does this indicate?
questions.explain: If the solution remains blue, no reducing sugar is present in the sample.

questions.q: A food gives a purple colour with biuret solution and a blue-black colour with iodine solution. Which nutrients does it contain?
questions.explain: Purple biuret indicates protein and blue-black iodine indicates starch.

questions.q: An unknown food substance is broken down into fatty acids and glycerol. Which type of nutrient was it?
questions.explain: Fats and oils are made from fatty acids and glycerol, so this substance is a fat.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610) syllabus; Biological Molecules
